investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle assertions required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct rejection reasons: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have Insufficient capacity — meaning the resource quota or the peer-pod provider limit for that resource type is exhausted — and (2) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints, making preemption unhelpful on all 6 nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122–145 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence to validate against the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 141s, 0/6 nodes available — same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion and affinity mismatch pattern.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 145s — confirms the condition persisted across the full eval window (18:23–18:31 UTC).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting and the runner never reaching VM readiness checks.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming no agent lifecycle data was returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod did not schedule.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call depends on a schedulable pod; if the pod is unschedulable the runner cannot collect any evidence.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130977, endedAt=2026-07-06T18:26:09.700Z — the check ran to its timeout without a successful pod start.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — the peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota, peer-pod operator slot limit) has no remaining capacity to allocate a new VM-backed pod, causing the scheduler to report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm.

[Likely contributing] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are at capacity, leaving no schedulable target in the 6-node cluster.

[Possible] A peer-pod operator or kata-containers runtime component on the 2 eligible nodes is unhealthy or has reduced its advertised resource count, making the nodes appear at capacity even if underlying cloud VMs are available.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node eviction reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than any single node can provide) could cause permanent Unschedulable status regardless of overall cluster load.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the probe pod. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are fully consumed (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod never scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned, and the probe timed out after ~141s without writing any required evidence fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary: Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, preventing fallback to the other 4 nodes even if they had general capacity.

Tertiary: A surge in concurrent remote agent creation (by real users or other eval runs) may have exhausted the limited VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes just before the eval window, causing a transient capacity crunch rather than a permanent shortage.

Lower confidence: The kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or reduced in count (e.g., a node was removed from the pool), shrinking available VM slots. No node-lifecycle evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle assertions required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct rejection reasons: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have Insufficient capacity — meaning the resource quota or the peer-pod provider limit for that resource type is exhausted — and (2) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints, making preemption unhelpful on all 6 nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122–145 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence to validate against the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 122s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 141s, 0/6 nodes available — same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion and affinity mismatch pattern.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 145s — confirms the condition persisted across the full eval window (18:23–18:31 UTC).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting and the runner never reaching VM readiness checks.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming no agent lifecycle data was returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod did not schedule.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call depends on a schedulable pod; if the pod is unschedulable the runner cannot collect any evidence.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130977, endedAt=2026-07-06T18:26:09.700Z — the check ran to its timeout without a successful pod start.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — the peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota, peer-pod operator slot limit) has no remaining capacity to allocate a new VM-backed pod, causing the scheduler to report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm.

[Likely contributing] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are at capacity, leaving no schedulable target in the 6-node cluster.

[Possible] A peer-pod operator or kata-containers runtime component on the 2 eligible nodes is unhealthy or has reduced its advertised resource count, making the nodes appear at capacity even if underlying cloud VMs are available.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node eviction reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than any single node can provide) could cause permanent Unschedulable status regardless of overall cluster load.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the probe pod. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are fully consumed (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod never scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned, and the probe timed out after ~141s without writing any required evidence fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary: Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, preventing fallback to the other 4 nodes even if they had general capacity.

Tertiary: A surge in concurrent remote agent creation (by real users or other eval runs) may have exhausted the limited VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes just before the eval window, causing a transient capacity crunch rather than a permanent shortage.

Lower confidence: The kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or reduced in count (e.g., a node was removed from the pool), shrinking available VM slots. No node-lifecycle evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 18:26 and 18:31 UTC on 2026-07-06 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence at all — every required field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is missing from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. Only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata peer-pod scheduling, and both report zero remaining capacity. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, the eval pod remains Pending until the probe timeout fires, producing a complete evidence gap and a check failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent feature's VM provisioning path; it is an eval failure against the production-api runtime environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads (from other eval runs, user sessions, or other cluster tenants) have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval pod.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and if those nodes are also resource-constrained, any capacity pressure immediately causes full scheduling failure with no fallback.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may have too few kata-capable nodes (only 2 of 6) relative to the concurrent demand for remote-agent pods, making the system fragile under any load spike.

Lower probability — a recent change to the pod spec's resource requests or node selector (not evidenced in suspectChanges, which is empty) could have tightened scheduling constraints, but no suspect commit is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible nodes to determine if slots are exhausted by live workloads or leaked/stuck pods from prior eval runs.
If leaked pods are found (e.g., prior eval runs that did not clean up), terminate them to free VM slots and re-run the eval to confirm recovery.

If slots are genuinely exhausted by concurrent demand, consider scaling the number of kata-capable nodes or increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on existing nodes to provide headroom for eval probes.

Review the pod's node affinity/selector to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional; if additional nodes could be made kata-capable, this would reduce the blast radius of any future capacity pressure.

Add a pre-flight check to the eval runner that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting remote agent creation, so the check can return a more actionable SKIP or WARN status instead of timing out.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the node affinity/selector mismatch hypothesis becomes primary.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held lock or a race condition during cleanup) rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check's pod spec rather than a shared VM capacity problem.

If a different scheduling error message appears (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota exceeded at namespace level) on re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need to be revised.
If no remote-agent pods are found in Pending state in the cluster, the scheduling failure may have been caused by a transient cluster event rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., via the Kubernetes API) and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add a pre-scheduling readiness check within the remote-agent-create eval that verifies at least one schedulable node exists before attempting agent creation, distinguishing infrastructure capacity failures from agent lifecycle failures.

Add a cluster-node-capacity check to the remote-agents feature group that runs before the three agent lifecycle checks and gates them, so a single infrastructure failure produces one clear signal rather than three cascading failures.

Consider adding a latency regression eval for remote-agent-create that alerts when pod scheduling time exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it reaches full Unschedulable status.
